title: Dependency ordering and makespan
prompt_text: Six tasks, each takes exactly one hour. Dependencies: extract and validate must both finish before transform; transform must finish before load and before features; load and features must both finish before publish. Two questions. First, if one worker runs the tasks one at a time, how many different valid orders are there? Second, with unlimited workers, what is the shortest wall-clock time to finish all six? Give both numbers and a brief justification.

Valid orders = 4. Explanation: P must be last; among first five, T must be third because only E,V can precede it and only L,F can follow it. E/V can be in 2! orders, L/F in 2! orders, so 2×2=4.

content:
Valid orders: **4**  
Shortest wall-clock time: **4 hours**

Brief justification:

- With one worker, **publish must be last**. Transform must come after both extract and validate, and before both load and features. So among the first five tasks, transform is exactly 3rd, extract/validate are the first two in either order, and load/features are the last two in either order:  
  \(2! \times 2! = 4\) valid orders.
- With unlimited workers, run extract and validate in parallel in hour 1, transform in hour 2, load and features in parallel in hour 3, and publish in hour 4. So the shortest time is **4 hours**.
